chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man experiences nocturnal emission and something touches his garment, he should wash the part that was touched; and if he thinks something touched it but is not certain and does not see its place, he should sprinkle it with water; and if he is certain that it touched it but does not see its place, he should wash his entire garment, for that is better.
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim purify his clothes after a nocturnal emission if the exact spot is unknown?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a graduated approach to ritual purity based on the certainty of impurity (najāsah), reflecting the Shia juristic principle of 'presumption of continuity' (istishāb) where doubt does not invalidate certainty. It highlights the practical application of removing physical impurity from garments, distinguishing between visible stains requiring washing, uncertain spots requiring sprinkling, and certain but unseen stains requiring full washing to ensure ritual validity for prayer.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man bed-wets, so something hits his clothes, then let him wash (that part) which has been hit; and if he thinks that something has hit is and is not certain and cannot see its place, so let him sprinkle it with the water; and if he is certain that it has hit it and cannot see its place, so let him wash his clothes, all of it, for it is better’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If a man experiences wet dream and his clothes come in contact with semen, he must wash the polluted area. If he thinks, but is not certain and has not seen the polluted area, he must pour water on it. If he is certain that semen has come in contact with his clothes but he has not seen the polluted spot, he must wash all of his clothes; it is better.’”
